terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where try.js runs your API on a clock it can move, signs Kofi out, and asks GET /me seven and eight hours after a sign-in.

tasks.title: Sign out
tasks.description:
Add `POST /sign-out` to the router in `src/routes/signIn.js`:

- remove the session of the request's session cookie from the store
- tell the browser to drop the session cookie: the same name and path, an empty value and a date in the past
- answer `204` with no body, also when the request had no session or one the store does not know
- end only that session: the same person signed in on another computer stays signed in

`sessionToken(req)` from `src/middleware/readSession.js` gives the value of the session cookie. The check signs out with sessions of its own, then sends `GET /me` with the old cookie and with others.
nextSteps: Add the route to the sign-in router.
Find the token and forget its session.
Tell the browser to drop the cookie.
hints: Signing out has two halves, like signing in: the server forgets the session, and the browser forgets the cookie. Only the first one is safety; the second is tidiness.
`sessions.remove(token)` forgets the server's half. `res.clearCookie(name, options)` sends the header that makes a browser drop a cookie.
`const token = sessionToken(req)`, then `if (token) sessions.remove(token)`, then `res.clearCookie('session', { httpOnly: true, sameSite: 'lax' })` and `res.status(204).end()`.

tasks.title: Give each session an end
tasks.description:
Give every new session an end, eight hours after it starts. In `POST /sign-in`:

- save `expiresAt` with the session: the time `now()` gives plus `SESSION_MS`, in milliseconds
- make the session cookie last as long: a `Max-Age` of eight hours
- keep the cookie HttpOnly, SameSite `Lax` and on the path `/`

Read the time only with `now()`, the clock `createApp` is given, never `Date.now()` itself. The check signs in with clocks of its own, then reads the session store and the `Set-Cookie` header.
nextSteps: Find where the session is saved and the cookie set.
Work out when the session ends, from `now()`.
Save that time with the session.
Give the cookie the same lifetime, then run `node try.js`.
hints: The server's record of the session and the browser's cookie each need to know when it ends.
`now()` gives milliseconds, like `Date.now()`. The `maxAge` option of `res.cookie()` is in milliseconds too, and Express writes the header's `Max-Age` in seconds for you.
`sessions.save(token, { staffId: member.id, expiresAt: now() + SESSION_MS })`, and `maxAge: SESSION_MS` among the cookie options.

tasks.title: Refuse a session that has ended
tasks.description:
Make `readSession(staff, sessions, now)` in `src/middleware/readSession.js` refuse a session that has ended:

- a session has ended once `now()` is at or past its `expiresAt`
- an ended session is removed from the store, and `req.staff` stays unset
- a session that has not ended works as before, and the request always goes on

The check saves sessions that end at times of its own, moves the clock, and sends `GET /me`, a change and a read.
nextSteps: Find where readSession looks up the session.
Compare its end with the time.
Forget a session that has ended.
Run `node try.js` and read the answer eight hours later.
hints: The cookie's `Max-Age` asks the browser to drop it, but a copied cookie can be sent for ever. Only the server can really end a session.
Compare `session.expiresAt` with `now()` right after the session is looked up. At exactly `expiresAt` it has ended.
Make `session` a `let`, then `if (session && session.expiresAt <= now()) { sessions.remove(token); session = undefined }` before the member is looked up.
